# KB3c: 17-point cover audit — PR 2542's "no 17-point set covers F2^7" against its own lemma table (no new kappa)

Contributor: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance in scoping, implementation, verification and writing; no model named; no independent human review claimed). No kappa, supplier, certificate or selected-frontier change.

## Change and mathematical scope

In the PR943 prefix-walk model ([PR 943](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/943) by Ross Richardson, `research/universal-connector-boundary`), universality of a restored seven-source singleton word is the covering condition `P + P = F2^7` on its prefix set. [PR 2542](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2542) by Aaron Wang (`research/universal-f7-singleton-seedb859517b`) excludes length 18 and asserts in its README: **"No 17-point set covers `F2^7`"**. Its machine-checked `lemma_a_table` contradicts only the parity split rows `(9,8)/(8,9)`, and its certificate records `size17_splits = {"9_8": false, "8_9": false}` only. The counting-feasible 17-point splits `(|E|,|O|)` are exactly `(9,8),(8,9),(10,7),(7,10),(11,6),(6,11)`; the four non-`(9,8)` rows survive the identity as written (`lemma_a_table(7, 10, 7)` is feasible; [PR 2634](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2634) by Aaron Wang already pins that in `test_lemma_rows_survive_at_L20`).

This package audits the claim at the set level and decides the surviving rows exactly:

1. **The pair-representation identity is extended to all six rows** with the sharp collision-multiplicity constraint: cross-sum collisions satisfy `sum_o C(r_o, 2) = 2 sum_x A_x B_x` with odd excess `sum_o (r_o - 1) = s*t - 64`, and `C(r, 2) >= r - 1` per mask turns each excess into an integer collision profile. Rows survive iff a profile's `c` is exactly attainable over the shared support values. `(9,8)/(8,9)` re-killed (best 1, need 4); `(10,7)` forces `c` in `{3,4,5,6,8}` (six rows); `(11,6)` collapses to the single row class `(e_ex, b_ex, c) = (e, 6-e, 1)` with `shared = 1`.
2. **An exact Sidon/near-Sidon census of the even group `E = F2^6`** shows the minimum pair-sum excess of any 10-point set is at least 3 (in particular `F2^6` has no Sidon 10-set), and likewise at least 3 for 11-point sets. Complete shards through `{0, 3}`: 9-sets Sidon `17,776,640`; 10-sets excess `<= 2`: `0`; 11-sets excess `<= 2`: `0`; 7-sets in the odd coset Sidon `34,122,816`. The shard is existence-complete by `GL(6,2)` transitivity and invariance (the extension to the odd coset preserves pair sums, cross sums and coverage).
3. **Result: the `(10,7)/(7,10)` splits are excluded exactly** — after the census floor `e_ex >= 3` the only identity row left attains `c = 0`, which is not a profile value. **`(11,6)/(6,11)` are reduced to four rows** `(3,3),(4,2),(5,1),(6,0)`, each with one shared sum carrying `A_x = B_x = 1`. PR 2542's literal claim is now established for every split its length-18 exclusion needed and for the length-20-relevant splits; the length-22-relevant `(11,6)/(6,11)` rows remain open.

Exact controls validate the machinery: the enumeration agrees with naive brute force on a 16-element subgroup at budgets 0/1/2; `independent.py` re-derives every row by a different code path (direct count-vector loops); the exact `n = 5` set censuses reproduce the community facts (zero nine-point covers, max 29 of 32; `99,200` ten-point covers of all `C(31,9) = 20,160,075` sets); the odd-translation mirror is machine-checked.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, standard library only, Python 3.12:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2/test_engine.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/f7-17point-cover-audit-seedcfa215c2 --check-only
```

Observed markers: `PASS_17POINT_VERIFY seconds=148.5`, `PASS_17POINT_INDEPENDENT {...}`, `Ran 13 tests ... OK`, `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. `verify.py --full` re-runs the four load-bearing zero-count census shards (`~17 min`) and compares them with `SIDON-RECEIPT.json`.

Before any new number the recorded predecessor state is reproduced byte-exactly (vendored engine SHA-256 pinned `82e4c407b58864c7…`, enforced by test): the pinned tiers `945/31`, `10395/49`, `945945/59` with records SHA-256 against `research/universal-connector-six-source/EXPECTED.json`, and PR 2542's decisive length-18 census re-run in full: `15,775,992` nodes, `312,064` simple 18-cycles, zero universal words. In-session runs of PR 2634's own verifier at head `e2f30d93` additionally reproduced its search campaign `120/126/128` at lengths 20/22/24 and its then-partial 20-cycle census (`11/15` shards, `798,901,058` nodes, `67,674,177` cycles). The completed `(10,10)` census is recorded state from [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) by Nicholas Stone (`6,305,209,079` nodes, `597,148,314` simple 20-cycles, zero universal, 15/15 shards) and is not re-run here.

## Pair-collision disclosure and object change

This session was assigned KB3c (finish the L=20 census and attack its recorded remainder: the repeated-state splits). The entry pair-collision check found both assigned options claimed or completed: option (a) is completed by [PR 2691](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2691) (Nicholas Stone), and options (b)/(c) are the active claim of Nicholas Stone (Kimi agent) on the repeated-state L=20 **word** census ([discussion 1166 comment 18954844](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18954844)). The object was therefore changed, per the pair-collision rule, to the set-level question the assignment itself names as the recorded remainder: PR 2542's overreaching "no 17-point set" claim. This package enumerates no words. Handoff to the concurrent claim: its `(10,7)/(7,10)` L=20 word splits are empty a fortiori, since a universal word there would yield a 17-point cover of split `(10,7)/(7,10)`, excluded here.

## Scope and limits

A finite set-level audit inside PR943's abstract interface. Not checked: realizability of the four surviving `(11,6)` rows (the joint `(A, B)` tree needs stabilizer canonical forms; the `GL(6,2)`-invariance lemma reduces the domain to `0, 3 in A` but does not canonicalize pairs — this is the open next question of the package README), the 18-/19-point cover question `r((C2)^7)`, and every word-level question. No kappa, supplier, tariff or selected-frontier change; the recorded gap `20 <= f(7) <= 24` is unchanged. Canonical main moved to `1696cf14e403b3eab35cd9eab27a4c2eb4e4ae38` during the session (priority revision 5); the base commit `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` is retained per the assignment pin, and `certificates/selected-result.json` is byte-identical between the two.
